title: AND Operator
description: Learn how to use the AND operator to combine multiple Boolean expressions in SQL Server.

data.alt: SQL Server AND multiple operators example

data.text: The AND operator is a logical operator that allows you to combine two Boolean expressions. It returns TRUE only when both expressions evaluate to TRUE.

data.title: AND Operator Syntax
data.content: Combine two Boolean expressions with AND.

data.text: The boolean_expression is any valid Boolean expression that evaluates to TRUE, FALSE, or UNKNOWN.
The following table shows the result when you combine TRUE, FALSE, and UNKNOWN values using the AND operator:

data.title: Operator Precedence
data.text: When you use more than one logical operator in an expression, SQL Server always evaluates the AND operators first. You can change the order of evaluation by using parentheses ().

data.title: Basic AND Example
data.content: Find products with category ID 1 and list price greater than 400.
data.code:
SELECT *
FROM production.products
WHERE
    category_id = 1
    AND list_price > 400
ORDER BY
    list_price DESC;

data.title: Multiple AND Operators
data.content: Find products with category ID 1, list price greater than 400, and brand ID 1.
data.code:
SELECT *
FROM production.products
WHERE
    category_id = 1
    AND list_price > 400
    AND brand_id = 1
ORDER BY
    list_price DESC;

data.text: The following example shows how to use the AND with the OR operator:

data.title: AND with OR
data.content: Due to precedence, AND is evaluated first: (brand_id=2 AND list_price>1000) OR brand_id=1.
data.code:
SELECT *
FROM production.products
WHERE
    brand_id = 1
    OR brand_id = 2
    AND list_price > 1000
ORDER BY
    brand_id DESC;

data.text: In this example, SQL Server evaluates the AND operator first. Therefore, the query retrieves products with brand ID 2 and list price greater than 1000, or brand ID 1.
To retrieve products with brand ID 1 or 2 AND a list price greater than 1000, you use parentheses:

data.title: AND with OR and Parentheses
data.content: Use parentheses to control evaluation order.
data.code:
SELECT *
FROM production.products
WHERE
    (brand_id = 1 OR brand_id = 2)
    AND list_price > 1000
ORDER BY
    brand_id;

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: The AND operator combines two Boolean expressions and returns TRUE only if both are TRUE.
AND has higher precedence than OR; use parentheses to control evaluation order.
AND returns FALSE if either expression is FALSE.
